explanation: Ozu often set his camera low, near the eye level of someone seated on a tatami mat. In 2012, Sight and Sound's poll of film directors voted Tokyo Story the best film ever made.

claims.text: Yasujirō Ozu directed Tokyo Story (1953), about an elderly couple who visit their grown-up children, who are too busy for them.
Akira Kurosawa, Kenji Mizoguchi and Masaki Kobayashi did not direct Tokyo Story.
Ozu often filmed from a low camera position, roughly the eye level of a person seated on a tatami mat.
In the 2012 Sight and Sound poll of film directors, Tokyo Story was voted the greatest film of all time.
